Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 4067 -1967 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
TUBE, SWAB (WEST TYPE), FOR THROAT 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 20 April 1967, after the draft finalized by the Medical Glass Instruments 
and Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer 
Products Division Council. 

0.2 Preparation of standards for surgical instruments, medical equipment and 
apparatus, including medical glass instruments has been taken up at the 
instance of the Advisory Committee for Development of Medical Instruments, 
Equipment and Appliances of the Government of India, 

0.3 Great need has been felt for the standardization of glass instruments 
used in pathological work. This standard covers such essential requirements 
as are expected to help in providing uniform equipment to all laboratories. 

0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on pathological 
glass apparatus. Other standards in the series are: 

IS : 3740-1966 Specification for tubes, glass, for pathological work 

IS : 3741-1966 Specification for tubes, sedimentation 

IS: 3742-1966 Specification for pipettes, dilution, for haemocyto- 

meters 
IS : 4068-1967 Specification for ureometer, Doremus type 
IS : 4069-1967 Specification for urinometer 
IS: 4087-1967 Specification for pipette for haemoglobinometer and 

pipette, blood, biochemical 

0.5 In the preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from 
IND/SL/MED/5849 ' Tube, swab (West), for throat' published by the 
Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 

0.6 This standard contains a clause which calls for agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier. The relevant clause is 7.1. 

0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing 
the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The 
number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the 
same as that of the specified value in this standard. 

♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 



IS:4067-1967 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This specification lays down the requirements for West type of swab 
tube for throat, used in pathological work. 

2. MATERIAL 

2*1 The tube shall be made from clear, neutral, heat-resistant glass tubing 
(for definitions see 18:1382-1961*). It shall pass the alkalinity test 
prescribed in IS : 2303-1963t for Type 1 glass. 

3. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The shape and dimensions of the tube shall be as given in Fig. 1. 

4. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

4.1 The tube shall be well annealed, free from bubbles and, as far as possible, 
free from striae, stones and other visible defects ( for definitions see IS : 1382- 
1961*). The tube shall pass the thermal shock test and dry heat test 
specified in 5.1 and 5.2 respectively. The two ends shall be at right angles 
to the tubing. The bend of the tube shall be smooth, regular and without 
any constriction. The two ends of the tube shall be smoothly rounded in the 
flame, 

5. TESTS 

5.1 Thermal Shock Test — The tube shall be first boiled in water for 
30 minutes and then transferred to water at about 20°C. It shall not show 
any chipping or cracking. 

5.2 Dry Heat Test — The tubes shall be subjected to a dry heat test in a 
sterilizing oven at 180° ± T'Qx for 30 minutes. The tubes shall show no 
deterioration in any way. 

6. MARKING 

6.1 The tube shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer, his 
initial or trade-mark. 

6.1.1 The tube may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

NoTB — The lise of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of tlie 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control 
during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by 
the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed arc 
continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under 
which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufac- 
turers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 



♦Glossary of terms relating to glass industry. 
' fMcthod of grading glass for alkalinity.

7. PACKING 

7.1 The tubes may be packed as given in 7.1.1 or as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. 

7.1.1 Each tube shall be wrapped in thin paper and suitably packed in a 
carton.
